messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Elevated latency + streaming stalls detected on /v1/stream/generate. Auto-threshold breached at 14:23 UTC. p95 ~ 1.2s (SLO 250ms), p99 ~ 3.1s, streaming stall count up 12x in last 5m. TTL/cache metrics flagged: prefix-cache miss rate jumped to ~82% (baseline ~6%).

Raj Patel: seeing it on the latency board too. linking dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/rt/streaming?orgId=1&from=-5m

Marta Li: quick snapshot from KV stats:
- prefix_hash_v2 rollout at 14:10 (canary -> all)
- prefix-hit-rate: 18% -> 4% since rollout
- eviction spikes on prefix-shards-7/8
- paging thundering: read latency for paging layer 50ms -> 800ms

Sam H: suspects prefix hash algorithm change caused key distribution mismatch + cache fragmentation. impact pattern = cold prefixes causing streaming stalls as KV fetches block.

Casey: confirmed an error cohort where streaming clients hit stall while waiting for paging read. stacktrace snippet in logs shows repeated KV timeouts: ```ERROR store/paging.go:137 fetchPrefix kv_timeout=1200ms key="pfx:usr:..."```

oncall-ops: I'm on it. Quick mitigation plan:
1) Roll back prefix-hash to v1 (hotfix rollback)
2) Increase in-memory fallback cache TTL and enable warmup job for hot prefixes
3) Reduce max batch size for streaming requests to lower tail amplification
4) Monitor p99 and streaming stall counts

Marta Li: adding telemetry view: p95/p99, prefix-miss-rate, paging-latency, streaming-stalls. Setting alert to page on further p99 increase.

Raj Patel: do we have a safe rollback command? Risk of cache misauth?

Casey: yes — rollout uses k8s configmap named prefix-hash-config. Rolling to previous commit:
```bash
kubectl set env deploy/prefix-service PREFIX_HASH_VERSION=v1 -n infra
kubectl rollout restart deploy/prefix-service -n infra
```
This keeps the same code, switches algorithm version flag. Will cause some transient churn but should restore key mapping.

oncall-ops: executing rollback now.

oncall-ops: running `kubectl set env`... output:
```
deployment.apps/prefix-service env updated
deployment "prefix-service" restarted
```

oncall-ops: restart complete, pods coming up. tailing logs...

telemetry-bot: Alert: prefix-miss-rate dropping from 82% -> 26% within 90s of rollback. paging read latency median down from 410ms -> 75ms.

Sam H: nice. streaming stalls reduced but p99 still elevated (1.1s). next step: kick off cache-warmup for top prefixes (recent hot keys).

Casey: warming hot prefixes using the adhoc job: ```/opt/tools/prefix_warm --source=recent-requests --top=2000 --concurrency=8``` 
Casey: job started, logs show warmup hit-rate improving for targeted shards.

Marta Li: customer-impact estimate: 0.9% of total requests experienced stall or timeouts in the window 14:10-14:40 UTC. Affected customers: two high-volume tenants saw visible degradations in synchronous endpoints; one support ticket opened (S-4217). No data loss, only latency and transient 5xx stream errors.

Raj Patel: any need for a model fallback? We can route critical customers to the smaller low-latency variant until fully recovered.

oncall-ops: enabled fallback-routing for the flagged tenants: routing policy update applied to route engine. Confirming no config drift.

telemetry-bot: p95 back to 230ms, p99 480ms. streaming-stalls down to baseline within 6m of warmup.

Sam H: recommend followups before close:
- run a canary rollout test to validate prefix-hash v2 changes against synthetic key distribution
- add stronger rollout guard (monitoring-based pause) to the CI/CD pipeline
- fix eviction/thundering by throttling warmup and ramping configmap change more gradually

Casey: filing a post-incident ticket with remediation actions and a playbook: https://tickets.redwood.ai/INC-9876. I'll attach logs, rollout diff, and warmup job details.

oncall-ops: handing off to next oncall (Sam H) for monitoring and followups. Summary: rollback of prefix-hash to v1 restored key distribution; warmup + fallback routing mitigated customer impact.

Sam H: taking handoff. I'll run the canary harness tomorrow morning and schedule a short retro. Thanks all :tada:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: latency and streaming stall counts returned to baseline. Severity: Sev2. Customer impact: limited latency degradation for ~30m window, one support ticket. Postmortem owner: Sam H.

Raj Patel: adding FYI to #postmortems and emailing affected customers with summary.

Marta Li: noted. Will add metric snapshots to the postmortem and include recommended rollout gating.

Casey: closing thread, leaving logs and traces attached to ticket. ping me if any anomalies reappear.

oncall-ops: next oncall acknowledged. :white_check_mark:
